feed.title: Decentralized Coinbase Payout Protocols (DCPP): A Framework for Discussion

entry.title: Decentralized Coinbase Payout Protocols (DCPP): A Framework for Discussion
entry.summary:
Sharechains possess the ability to support flexible payout configurations without constraining all participants to the limitations of the least powerful machine in the pool. By leveraging the fact that Stratum operates locally on each node, a unique coinbase transaction can be generated for every miner connected to a node. This setup allows for dynamic adjustment in coinbase sizes, accommodating different levels of mining contribution.
When a share is discovered, validation rules evolve from requiring an exact match of the coinbase to accepting variations that align with the dynamically generated coinbases. The existence of a valid share indicates that an ASIC accepted the corresponding coinbase and, provided the system adheres to Pay-Per-Last-N-Shares (PPLNS) and established reward distribution protocols, such shares are considered legitimate contributions.
One potential concern arises regarding whether this flexibility could introduce strategic behaviors. Specifically, there is a risk that certain nodes might consistently mine only a limited number of slots that pay exclusively to their own addresses. This scenario raises questions about the possibility of exacerbating Relative Luck Attack (RLA) vulnerabilities, as it may allow some participants to optimize their payouts at the expense of the broader pool. Further scrutiny is essential to ensure that reward mechanisms remain fair and resistant to manipulation in light of these operational changes.
